    Projective modules are Euler-projective #

    Euler-projectivity is invariant under isomorphism (EulerProj.of_bijective) and holds for a module once it holds for the summands of a decomposition (EulerProj.of_decomp). Sums of indecomposable projectives decompose into them (decompSumProj), so by the Krull–Schmidt step every indecomposable summand of such a sum is some A e, and every direct summand of a sum of indecomposable projectives is Euler-projective (eulerProj_of_summand).

              theorem LargeIndecomposable.AR.euler_eq_hom_of_pd_one {k A : Type u} [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (D : DirData k A) (hT : ∀ (x : D.ι), x ∈ D.T) {Z W : FDMod k A} (L : List ((i : D.ι) × ↥(eSub Z (D.e i)))) (hL : Function.Surjective ⇑(sumMap D Z L)) (l : List D.ι) (s : FDMod.ofSub (sumMap D Z L).ker ⟶ sumProj D l) (r : sumProj D l ⟶ FDMod.ofSub (sumMap D Z L).ker) (hsr : CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp s r = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id (FDMod.ofSub (sumMap D Z L).ker)) (hv : ExtVanish Z W) :
              euler D (dimZ D Z) (dimZ D W) = ↑(Module.finrank k (Z.carrier →ₗ[A] W.carrier))

              The Euler form of a rigid module of projective dimension at most one. If the kernel of a cover of Z by indecomposable projectives is a direct summand of a sum of indecomposable projectives, and every extension of Z by W splits, then ⟨dim Z, dim W⟩ = dim Hom(Z, W).
